description: SYNTHETIC reference device. No such board exists; the values are illustrative and chosen to exercise the schema. Board and firmware claims are 'declared' because there is no hardware to measure -- a real profile must replace them with 'measured' ones carrying procedures.

lead_off_freq_divisor.note: FLEAD_OFF[1:0]=11 selects fDR/4. The carrier tracks the sample rate; it is not a fixed physical frequency.

decimation_response.note: Third-order sinc decimation, sinc^3(f/fs). A function of f/fs, so carrier attenuation is the same constant at every rate.

carrier_slope_uv_per_kohm.note: Illustrative. A real value needs a two-point resistor ladder.

carrier_intercept_uv.note: Illustrative zero. Do not assume a real board's intercept is zero -- that assumption is what a single-point calibration silently makes.

analogue_pole_hz.note: None modelled. On a real board 'absent' is itself a measurement, not a default.

uv_scale_factor.note: Declared by the firmware author as already input-referred. Verify against a known differential input before trusting it; see conformance/test_profile_contract.py.

interference_lines_hz.note: Explicit list. MUST NOT be derived from the sample rate.

channel_order.note: CSV column order. Readers select positionally; header labels are not evidence.

carrier_amplitude_convention.note: The chip's sinc^3 decimation removes the injected square wave's harmonics, so the carrier arrives near-sinusoidal and the sine conversion is the physically correct one.

analysis_rate_hz.note: 500/4. Integer factor from this device's source rate.

epoch_gates.note: PLACEHOLDER values for the synthetic reference device. Real thresholds must be derived from labelled artefact recordings on the device in question. A threshold tuned until the output looks reasonable has been fitted to the answer -- see spec/40-processing.md R-40.12.
